key_insight: Physics constraints only remain valid after coarse-graining if they are linear and closed on the filtered fields; otherwise, enforcing the raw PDE can bake in a wrong closure.
engineering_relevance: For turbulent-flow surrogates, a cheap projection can enforce continuity and momentum exactly, improving rollout stability far more efficiently than test-time optimization or naive physics losses.
method: Train a Fourier neural operator on coarse, stochastically forced turbulence data.
Apply a closed-form Fourier-space projection to enforce continuity and global momentum balance at O(N log N) cost.
For nonlinear balances, fit a constant subgrid flux from coarse training data to close the energy constraint.
evidence_signal: On 2D turbulence, the projection reduced continuity error to 5.0e-7 and momentum-balance error to 8.6e-11, while raising bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on Kolmogorov flow, it was about 3300x cheaper than test-time optimization.
watch_item: The approach depends on identifying constraints that remain closed after filtering; unmodeled nonlinear subgrid effects can still invalidate a direct physics loss.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
